title: Nibbles and the Wobbly Ducklings
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a cosy burrow, lived a little hamster named Nibbles. His home was super neat. Nuts were stacked in little towers, tiny stones were sorted by size, and his fluffy bedding was always smooth. Nibbles had the softest cheeks, always puffed out as if he had snacks for days. Every day was the same for Nibbles. He’d wake up with the sun, tidy his burrow, and munch a crunchy carrot while listening to birds sing. It was a peaceful life. But sometimes, when happy robins sang with busy bees, Nibbles would peek out his window. He’d watch the little birds fly by in pairs, and a quiet thought would tickle his chest: his orderly world would be even nicer with a friend to share his adventures.

Until one day, the sky above the park put on a hat of fluffy grey clouds. A soft playful breeze whispered secrets to the leaves. Nibbles, always curious, wiggled his nose and peeked outside. And what did he see? A wobbly yellow parade. It was a group of little ducklings, and they looked a little bit worried. Each one held a small leaf flag that fluttered. The tiniest duckling, no bigger than a puff of dandelion fluff, waddled right up to Nibbles’ door. “Excuse me, Mr Hamster?” he peeped, his voice as small as his feet. “We need to get to the big splashy pond before the rain starts to patter, but we don’t know the way. It’s a long trip for our little webbed feet.”

Nibbles felt a funny flutter in his tummy. It wasn’t a scared feeling, more like an oh-my-whiskers, an adventure flutter. Nibbles was great at tidying, but big adventures? Not so much. Still, the ducklings looked so ready and so very, very cute. He knew just who could help with a long journey and lots of fun. With a determined wiggle of his nose, Nibbles scampered as fast as his little legs could go to the edge of the sparkly river. There, with a cheerful splash, lived his best friend, Splash the dolphin. Splash had a sleek bright blue body that shone like a shiny jewel, and his smile was as wide and bubbly as the river.

“Splash,” squeaked Nibbles, full of excitement. “I have a super important job for us. A whole parade of the most adorable ducklings needs our help to get across the park to the big pond before the rain begins.”

Splash leaped out of the water with a happy flip, sending tiny rainbow drops into the air. “A job. Hooray. Adventures are my favourite. Lead the way, my neat friend Nibbles.”

Because of that, Nibbles and Splash set off. Nibbles, with his clever hamster nose, trotted ahead, twitching his whiskers to show the way. Splash, with his strong tail, swam happily next to the river that wound through the park. He kept a watchful friendly eye on the little ducklings. Soon they came to a tiny bridge made of twigs and moss. It looked a little wobbly, and the ducklings stopped, quacking softly. “Oh dear,” peeped one. “It looks a bit wiggly.”

Nibbles puffed out his chest, feeling quite brave. “Don’t worry,” he called. “Splash can help.” Splash nudged the wobbly bridge very, very gently with his smooth nose. It didn’t shake or wobble anymore. It felt much steadier, like a big friendly hug. Nibbles then showed the ducklings how to take small careful steps, one after another, wibble-wobbling their way across. They held their little leaf flags high and kept going, their soft quacks filling the air.

Their journey continued, following a path with sunny patches peeking through the leaves. But oh no. The path ahead was covered in big floppy colourful leaves. The ducklings couldn’t see where to put their little webbed feet. Nibbles, with his super sniffer, sniffed the air and then the ground, finding the clearest path through the leafy carpet. “Follow me, little ones,” he chirped, his voice full of helpfulness. Splash, with his big wide friendly smile, whistled a happy bubbly tune that made the ducklings feel extra brave and ready for anything. They giggled with delight as they waddled through the soft rustling leaves, feeling like they were walking on a giant cosy blanket.

Until finally, a wonderful sound reached their ears — a happy splashing sound. They had reached the big pond. The sky, which had been a soft grey, began to sprinkle the very first, softest drops of rain. They were fat friendly raindrops, like little kisses from the sky, carrying the fresh clean smell of damp earth. The ducklings cheered with excited little quacks and happily paddled into the warm welcoming water, safe and sound and oh-so-pleased. Nibbles and Splash sat together under the wide friendly umbrella of a giant mushroom, watching the ducklings swim and play. They felt warm and happy inside, a happy glow that was even better than a perfectly stacked nut.

Ever since that day, Nibbles the hamster, who loved order, and Splash the dolphin, who loved fun, set off together whenever a wobbly parade needed a path. The nut towers still stood. The stones stayed sorted. And the window, when Nibbles peeked, no longer looked quite so empty.
